item.title: CIR/02/2024: Research Manager (m/f/d)
item.description:
We combine excellence in research, teaching, and patient care. The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is a maximum care hospital with more than 1,300 beds. With around 38 clinics and 31 institutes as well as more than 8,000 employees (over 5,000 full-time staff), the UKB is one of the largest employers in Bonn. Every year, the UKB treats around 50,000 inpatients and around 35,000 emergencies, as well as provides over 350,000 outpatient treatments.

The following part-time (33%) Research Manager position is available at the Computational Imaging Research (CIR) Lab, led by Prof. Dr. Shadi Albarqouni, in the Clinic for Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology of the University Hospital Bonn, University of Bonn:

Research Manager (m/f/d)

starting Nov 2024 or as agreed upon. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of extension.

The Research Manager will work within the newly founded Computational Imaging Research (CIR) Lab, which focuses on developing:

  1. Fully automated, highly accurate computational methods to overcome challenges in medical imaging, including limited annotated data, low inter-/intra-observer agreement, inter-/intra-scanner variability, and domain shifts.
  2. Innovative Federated Learning algorithms that enable robust, privacy-preserved knowledge sharing among AI agents.
  3. Affordable AI solutions tailored for low-quality data from low-resource settings and point-of-care devices.

Your responsibilities:

  • Overseeing and coordinating research projects within the CIR Lab.
  • Managing project timelines, deliverables, and communications with internal teams and external collaborators.
  • Facilitating the data collection, annotation processes, and quality control of imaging data.
  • Supporting grant writing, reporting, and funding applications for ongoing and future projects.
  • Supervising research staff, including assisting with onboarding and training.
  • Ensuring adherence to ethical guidelines and regulatory requirements in research projects.
  • Acting as the main point of contact between clinical partners, lab members, and other stakeholders.

Your qualifications:

  • Educational Background: A Ph.D. in Medical Imaging, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field, with strong experience in research project management. A Medical Doctorate (MD) or Medical Science backgrouns with research management experience is also acceptable.
  • Project Management Experience: Proven experience in managing and coordinating research projects, particularly in an academic or healthcare setting.
  • Research Interest: A passion for medical imaging, AI applications, and a track record of involvement in relevant research.
  • Team Leadership: Strong leadership skills, with the ability to mentor and guide a multidisciplinary team.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Excellent organizational, interpersonal, and communication skills, capable of handling collaboration between various departments and institutions.
  • Technical Skills: Knowledge of Machine Learning or Deep Learning frameworks, as well as familiarity with medical imaging tools.
  • Language Skills: Fluent in English; knowledge of German is preferred but not required.

What we offer you:

  • A secure future: remuneration according to the German salary scale TV-L E13 (part-time, 33%).
  • Flexible for families: flexible working hours, the option of home office, onsite nursery, and parental care services.
  • Provisions for later: company pension scheme.
  • Discounted public transport ticket: discounted ticket for public transport (VRS).
  • Health services: on-site health management with numerous health promotion offers.
  • Employer benefits: Discounted offers for employees.
  • Subsidized continuing education and training.

The University of Bonn is committed to diversity and equal opportunity and is certified as a family-friendly university. It aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where women are under-represented and to promote their careers in particular. Therefore, we strongly encourage applications from qualified women. Applications will be handled in accordance with the State Equality Act (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz). Applications from individuals with a certified severe disability and from those of equal status are particularly welcome.

Contact:

If you meet the requirements and you are looking for a challenging job? Do not hesitate and send your application including a cover letter (highlighting your qualifications), a detailed CV (with links to previous projects and code), scanned academic degrees, and the contact details of two referees (preferably by e-mail in a single PDF file up to 5 MB in size), quoting the job advertisement no. CIR/02/2024 in your application.

item.title: AGYA/03/2024: Multiple Research Assistant Openings in Machine/Deep Learning for Interdisciplinary AI Research (m/f/d)
item.description:
Arab-German Young Academy of Sciences and Humanities (AGYA)
AGYA is based at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (BBAW) and at the Academy of Scientific Research and Technology (ASRT) in Egypt. It was established in 2013 as the first bilateral young academy worldwide. AGYA promotes research cooperation among outstanding early-career researchers (3–10 years after Ph.D.) from all disciplines who are affiliated with a research institution in Germany or any Arab country. The academy supports the innovative projects of its members in various fields of research as well as in science policy and education. To date, AGYA members have developed and carried out more than 150 interdisciplinary projects in over 60 cities and 30 countries. The diverse projects have dealt with topics relevant to society, such as scarcity of resources, public health, migration, education, and cultural heritage protection. AGYA is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and various Arab cooperation partners.

The following Research Assistant (Machine/Deep Learning) are available within the scope of funded projects by AGYA, led by Prof. Dr. Shadi Albarqouni:

Multiple Research Assistant Openings in Machine/Deep Learning for Interdisciplinary AI Research (m/f/d)

starting mid. Oct 2024 or as agreed upon. Service Contracts are limited to 3 months, with a possiblilty of an extension. The applicant must be based either in Arab nation or Europe.

These Service Contracts are part of newly funded interdisciplinary research projects through AGYA. The projects aim to leverage Machine and Deep Learning techniques to address diverse societal and scientific challenges, including:

  • Stress Detection in Olive Trees: Using AI to monitor and quantify stress indicators in olive crops.
  • Polyphenols Quantification in Pomegranate: Developing machine learning models to quantify polyphenols in pomegranate using spectral and imaging data.
  • Bacterial Colonies Detection and Classification in Water Samples: Applying advanced AI models to identify and classify bacterial colonies in water quality monitoring.
  • Classification and Segmentation in Medical Imaging: Using AI to enhance the accuracy and precision of medical imaging tasks.

Your responsibilities:

  • Develop machine learning algorithms for interdisciplinary applications, such as stress detection in agriculture, chemical quantification, and medical imaging.
  • Design and implement deep learning models for data classification, segmentation, and quantification.
  • Develop robust algorithms for adversarial attack resistance and model interpretability.
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to understand problem domains and optimize AI solutions.
  • Publish and present scientific outcomes at international conferences and high-impact journals.

Your qualifications:

  • B.Sc./M.Sc. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or equivalent with an interest in interdisciplinary AI research.
  • Strong knowledge of Machine/Deep Learning with experience in discriminative models, adversarial attacks, and Bayesian neural networks.
  • Excellent programming skills in Python and experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, including fundamental software engineering principles and machine learning design patterns.
  • Excellent analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Highly motivated and a team player with excellent communication and presentation skills, including experience in communicating across discipline boundaries.
  • Fluent command of the English language.

What we offer you:

  • A service contract by the Arab-German Young Academy for Sciences and Humanities (AGYA)

AGYA is committed to diversity and equal opportunity. We aim to increase the proportion of women in areas where women are under-represented and promote their careers. Therefore, we strongly encourage applications from qualified women. Applications from individuals with a certified severe disability and those of equal status are particularly welcome.

Contact:

If you meet the requirements and are looking for a challenging opportunity to work on interdisciplinary AI research, do not hesitate to send your application, including a cover letter (highlighting your qualifications), a detailed CV (with links to previous projects and code), scanned academic degrees, and the contact details of two referees (preferably by e-mail in a single PDF file up to 5 MB in size), quoting the job advertisement no. AGYA/03/2024 in your application.

item.description:
Arab-German Young Academy of Sciences and Humanities (AGYA)
AGYA is based at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (BBAW) and at the Academy of Scientific Research and Technology (ASRT) in Egypt. It was established in 2013 as the first bilateral young academy worldwide. AGYA promotes research cooperation among outstanding early-career researchers (3–10 years after Ph.D.) from all disciplines who are affiliated with a research institution in Germany or any Arab country. The academy supports the innovative projects of its members in various fields of research as well as in science policy and education. To date, AGYA members have developed and carried out more than 150 interdisciplinary projects in over 60 cities and 30 countries. The diverse projects have dealt with topics relevant to society, such as scarcity of resources, public health, migration, education, and cultural heritage protection. AGYA is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and various Arab cooperation partners.

The following Research Assistant (Software Developer) is available within the scope of a funded project by AGYA, led by Prof. Dr. Shadi Albarqouni:

Research Assistant (Software Developer) in AI for Interdisciplinary Research (m/f/d)

starting mid. Oct 2024 or as agreed upon. The Service Contract is limited to 3 months, with a possiblilty of an extension. The applicant must be based either in Arab nation or Europe.

This Service Contract is part of a newly funded interdisciplinary research project through AGYA. The project aims to leverage Artificial Intelligence to tackle challenges in various domains, including healthcare, agriculture, and cultural heritage protection. Specifically, the Arab-German Young Academy of Sciences and Humanities (AGYA) is facilitating cutting-edge research in collaboration with scientists and institutions across Germany and Arab countries, fostering impactful solutions for societal challenges.

The Research Assistant will focus on developing a GDPR-compliant telemedicine application, incorporating advanced imaging features and machine learning (ML) integration. The candidate will work on image data handling, secure storage, and ML model integration for medical image analysis. Additionally, the app will be expanded to communicate further disease information and treatment details to patients based on publicly available health resources.

Your responsibilities:

  • Develop a GDPR-compliant mobile telemedicine application that supports image uploads (via camera and file selection) and PDF reading.
  • Implement secure data transmission between the app and an ML server for inference (e.g., prediction or quantification), and integrate the diagnostic results into the app.
  • Collaborate with clinicians to ensure correct medical imaging and clinical information integration.
  • Implement user-friendly features to allow patients to receive follow-up educational information about their diagnosis using publicly available healthcare resources.
  • Use no-code/low-code platforms to expedite development while ensuring the scalability and robustness of the application.
  • Maintain secure data handling and storage practices in line with GDPR regulations.
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary research teams and domain experts to ensure the application’s functionality aligns with healthcare and other domain requirements.

Your qualifications:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • Proven experience in mobile app development using no-code/low-code platforms (e.g., Bubble, Adalo, Mendix).
  • Strong knowledge of secure data handling practices, with experience in GDPR compliance.
  • Familiarity with machine learning integration for medical image analysis (e.g., REST APIs, GraphQL).
  • Excellent programming skills in mobile development, particularly with frameworks like Flutter or React Native.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with interdisciplinary teams, including healthcare professionals.
  • Fluent command of the English language.

Desirable qualifications:

  • Experience in healthcare or telemedicine app development.
  • Familiarity with image processing, ML models, and secure database integration.
  • Experience in developing applications that include educational components for end-users.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and an eye for user-friendly design.

What we offer you:

item.title: CIR/03/2024: Postdoc/Research Staff position in Computational Medical Imaging (m/f/d)
item.description:
We combine excellence in research, teaching, and patient care. The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is a maximum care hospital with more than 1,300 beds. With around 38 clinics and 31 institutes as well as more than 8,000 employees (over 5,000 full-time staff), the UKB is one of the largest employers in Bonn. Every year, the UKB treats around 50,000 inpatients and around 35,000 emergencies, as well as provides over 350,000 outpatient treatments.

The following full-time (38.5 hrs./week) Psotdcotoral researcher position is available at the Computational Imaging Research (CIR) Lab, headed by Prof. Dr. Shadi Albarqouni, in the Clinic for Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology of the University Hospital Bonn, University of Bonn:

Postdoc/Research Staff position in Computational Medical Imaging (m/f/d)

starting Nov. 2024 or as agreed upon. The position is initially limited to two years.

The Postdoc/Research Staff position will be based in the newly founded research lab for Computational Imaging Research (CIR), which aims to develop i) fully automated, highly accurate innovative computational methods that save expert labor and efforts, and mitigate the challenges in medical imaging; namely the availability of a few annotated data, low inter-/intra-observers agreement, inter-/intra-scanners variability and domain shift, ii) innovative deep Federated Learning algorithms that can fairly distill and share the knowledge among AI agents in a robust and privacy-preserved way, and iii) affordable AI algorithms suitable for low-quality data generated by low-resource settings and point-of-care. The Postdoc/Research Staff will have the chance to closely work with clinicians and Ph.D. students on two funded projects; DFG Project on Robustness and Uncertainty in MRI-guided Radiotherapy and the other one on developing a clinical use-case for the MII Project on Open Medical Interface (OMI). If you have experience with computational methods in medical imaging, this is a great opportunity to be part of our team.

Your responsibilities:

  • Develop innovative computational algorithms for Robustness and Uncertainty
  • Publish and present scientific outcomes at Intl. conferences and high-impact journals
  • Maintain close collaboration with the team members and clinical partners

Your qualifications:

  • M.Sc./Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or equivalent with an interest in Medical Imaging
  • Strong knowledge in Machine/Deep Learning with experience in discriminative and generative models, robustness, and uncertainty quantification.
  • Track record of publications at top-tier conferences in the field (e.g., MICCAI, IPMI, and MIDL) and high-impact journals in the field (e.g., Nat. Mach. Intell., MedIA, and IEEE TMI)
  • Excellent programming skills in Python, PyTorch, and MONAI including fundamental software engineering principles and machine learning design patterns
  • Working in a Linux environment, with experience in shell and cluster (SLURM) scripting
